title: GPU Pool Capacity Control Panel — scaling policy editor & burst safety UX
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an integrated control panel for Dedicated GPU pools that combines health signals, scaling policy editing, and burst safety controls into a single surface. This ticket covers low-fidelity and high-fidelity prototypes, interaction specs for the scaling policy DSL, and a review-ready Figma file for PM/Eng sign-off. Primary goals: make autoscale behavior discoverable, reduce configuration errors, and provide clear fallback/rollback affordances for burst incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with desktop and tablet variants linked in design_links
Interaction spec describing policy precedence, cooldowns, min/max, and burst budgets
Accessible color contrast and keyboard-first interactions for policy editor panels
Engineering intake doc (Confluence) with component list and API hooks
decisions: Single-page control panel vs. multi-tab: chose single-page with collapsible sections to keep context during incident workflows
Burst mode modeled as a consumable budget tied to pool and tenant level — visible meter in header
Expose policy fields: min_replica, max_replica, target_latency_ms, sample_window_s, cooldown_s, burst_budget_units
tradeoffs: Placing too many knobs in primary view risks cognitive overload; addressed with progressive disclosure and presets
Automatically recommending quantized presets vs. manual entry — opted to provide recommended presets with a one-click apply and explainers rather than enforced automation
Showing real-time metrics can increase load on the console; we use a 5s polling rate for live incidents and static 1m snapshots for normal view
review_comments: PM (Jordan Patel): request to add an explicit 'simulate policy' CTA to run synthetic traffic for preview
Eng (Nadia Ortiz): prefer exposing a normalized burst_units metric and backend conversion docs — added to engineering intake
Security (Arjun Singh): ensure RBAC gates for burst override and rollout actions — flagged as must-have for release
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi components and handoff tokens (colors, spacing, iconography)
Create engineering intake with API contract and mocked responses
Schedule design review with runtime and infra leads (target 2025-03-15)
Prepare accessibility audit checklist and keyboard flow videos
